name: Bois Brule River (Brule River State Forest)
gaugeName: BOIS BRULE RIVER AT BRULE, WI
blurb: The Bois Brule River through the Brule River State Forest between WDNR designated canoe landings, with WDNR times between landings.

timing.note: A reviewed speed/flow calibration has not been established. Access and guide information remain available.

sections.notes: Markers identify agency-listed access; the map states whether a landing or an approximate facility area has been reviewed. Mileage is preliminary, measured along USGS river geometry; it is not a surveyed paddling route. Difficulty has not been independently rated for every section. Check current conditions, hazards and access with the managing agency before paddling.

notices.title: No inflatables or motorized boats on these sections
notices.text: Use a permitted canoe or kayak and designated canoe landings. DNR prohibits inflatables and motors here; its motor exception is only within one mile of the Lake Superior mouth, outside these sections.
notices.sourceName: Wisconsin DNR — paddling the Bois Brule

notices.title: Distance needs confirmation
notices.text: Wisconsin DNR describes Stone Chimney to Stones Bridge as 4.5 miles, while the imported geometry gives 2.5 miles. Confirm the intended Stone Chimney landing and channel before relying on the listed mileage.

notices.title: River hazard
notices.text: WDNR Brule River State Forest: "More adventurous folks can stay on the river another 45 minutes and experience Little Joe Rapids, a modest class II rapids located just upstream of the Bois Brule canoe landing."
